answer_text:
Interpreting “the splitting field of \(x^n-1\)” in the usual cyclotomic sense over \(\mathbb{Q}\), take

\[
\mathbb{F}_2=\{0,1\}.
\]

This is a finite field of characteristic \(2\). For every integer \(n\), the splitting field of \(x^n-1\) over \(\mathbb{Q}\) is a cyclotomic field \(\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_n)\), which has characteristic \(0\). Therefore \(\mathbb{F}_2\) cannot be such a splitting field for any \(n\).

Thus the characteristic is

\[
\boxed{2}
\]

Remark: if the intended base field were the prime subfield \(\mathbb{F}_p\) of the finite field, then no such example exists, since every finite field \(\mathbb{F}_{p^m}\) is the splitting field of \(x^{p^m-1}-1\) over \(\mathbb{F}_p\).
